experiments.scope: Reduced event on the selected Orchard Poseidon target at its own round count: the first 14 bits of the big-endian reading of the 32-byte digest agree for two distinct canonical messages. One birthday search per organizer trial over fresh inputs from the trial seed. No full collision is expected or claimed.
experiments.hypothesis: A search of at most 1200 fresh inputs returns a pair whose digests agree on those 14 bits in every trial. The count of trials that return a pair is a reproducible observation; no probability, rate or population bound is drawn from it (public organizer seeds; nothing is assumed about the seeded trials being independent or identically distributed). Checks the digest of the selected target at one reduced width; it says nothing about the full-width map, the cost or the success probability.

experiments.scope: Euclidean normality of the algorithm's own construction at reduced depth, on the selected Orchard Poseidon target (proof.md 9.5, 10.5.1). Two centres per trial, the first from the trial seed, the second from the seed and its index. For each centre c the program builds F_2(c + X), the coordinate 0 after the first 2 S-box layers on the line j = 0 of the first two rounds (the F_N of proof.md 10.3, degree 25), its monic odd part g about c (degree m = 12), R = X^((p-1)/2) mod g and the complete Euclidean remainder sequence of (g, R - 1), exactly over F_p. All 256 trials are computed, 512 sequences. A trial whose two sequences are both normal (deg(R - 1) = m - 1 and every quotient of degree 1 down to the gcd) and pass the self-checks returns two distinct canonical messages on the line whose digests agree on the first 6 bits, found among 65 line points (certain, by pigeonhole); any other trial returns two nulls. The final letter of the id only changes the organizer seeds. No full collision is expected or claimed.
experiments.hypothesis: Every computed sequence is normal, so exactly 256 of the 256 trials return a pair and the abnormal count is zero in 512 sequences. Per trial the program reports the untrusted observations sequences, normal_sequences, selfcheck_ok, abnormal_quotients, gcd_positive and max_quotient_degree. Zero abnormal sequences is reported as a reproducible observation consistent with H-NORMAL; the organizer-seeded centres are not treated as independent unselected samples and no population bound is drawn from them (delta = 0.003 is the declared premise). Supports the premise H-NORMAL of proof.md 9.5 at m = 12 on the construction's own pairs; it says nothing about the scale m of the claim, the cost or the success probability.
